# Authoring this ArchMeta repository

**Generated by the ArchMeta Kernel from this repository's own metamodels.**
Do not edit it; it is rewritten whenever the vocabulary changes. It exists so an
AI assistant can author this repository correctly instead of guessing.

## How to work here

1. Write or edit the `.arch` files in this repository.
2. The Kernel reloads them.
3. **Read `archmeta-report.md`** — every unresolved reference, unknown type and
   malformed attribute is listed there with its file and line. `archmeta-report.json`
   is the same thing in a form you can parse.
4. Fix what it names, and repeat.

Nothing you write can break the repository. A statement the Kernel cannot
understand costs that statement and becomes a diagnostic; the rest still loads.
So prefer writing the whole file and reading the report over writing timidly.

## The language

```
element <name> {
  type "<type>"
  description "free text"
}

relationship <name> {
  source <element>
  target <element>
  type "<type>"
}
```

- **Every relationship statement carries a name**, written after `relationship`
  (in `.data`, as a `name` line inside the block). Use `<source>-<type>-<target>`:
  the endpoints with their dots turned into `-`, and the type's local name —
  `orders.api` using `c4:uses` towards `billing` is `orders-api-uses-billing`. If
  that name is already held by an element or a relationship, add `-2`, `-3`, … An
  unnamed relationship is reported as `relationship-unnamed`.
- A name is a dotted path. `orders.api` is an identifier, and nothing more —
  **the dots do not create a hierarchy** in `.arch`.
  Nesting comes from a containment relationship: `c4:holds`, `core:holds`, marked below.
- Identifiers are case-insensitive, and every element has exactly one parent.
- File organisation is free. Which file a thing lives in never changes its identity,
  so group by whatever makes the model readable.

## Linking a file

`description-file`, `bpmn-file` and `sequence-file` name a file of this repository.
Write its **bare file name** (`cap-tiers.md`) when no other file in the repository has
that name, otherwise its **full path from the repository root** (`model/elements/capabilities/cap-tiers.md`).
Never a path relative to the file you are writing: the Kernel reads every path from the
repository root, so `capabilities/cap-tiers.md` written in `model/elements/apps.arch` names a file
that does not exist.

## Files you must not edit

- `archmeta-report.md` and `.json`, `archmeta-organisation.md` and `.json`, and this
  file. All written by the Kernel.
- `.view` files hold diagram layout — which elements are on a diagram and where.
  They are written by the Viewer when someone arranges a diagram. Editing the model
  is what you are here for; leave the layout alone unless asked.

`.md` description files and `.bpmn` diagrams are authoritative: the Kernel never
rewrites them, so they are yours to edit freely.

A `.sequence` file holds one sequence diagram (`sequence <name> { participant <element> ... message <from> -> <to> }`);
an element attaches it with `sequence-file "<file>"`. The Viewer rewrites the file when someone saves the sequence there.
